title: Fees waived by ordinance
question: Which fees has the Board waived, ended or refunded by ordinance since 2018, and what do the documents say that cost?
finding: 84 ordinances passed since 2018 waive, end, reduce or refund a fee, or forgive rent: fee waived (62); fee ended (8); fee reduced (7); fee refunded (4); rent forgiven (3). Dollars are on file for one programme. The Board’s analyst reported that First Year Free, which waives first-year permit, licence and registration fees for small businesses, waived $1,649,977 in fiscal 2022-23 and $1,564,250 in the first ten months of 2023-24 (about $1,877,101 for the year), had enrolled 7,467 businesses by June 17, 2024, and would cost about $30.3 million over ten years if made permanent; it also noted a plan to waive about $10 million in licence fees. For the other ordinances the titles name the fee but not the sum. What each permit fee is, and how fees changed, is in the site’s “What the rulebook requires” page.
how: Every ordinance passed from 2018 to November 2026 whose short or long title speaks of waiving, eliminating, repealing, reducing or refunding a fee, or forgiving rent, newest first. “In its own words” is the clause of the long title that holds those words, cut to 25 words. The dollar figures are read from the Budget and Legislative Analyst’s report of 28 June 2024.
limits: A fee waiver passed by ordinance is a public decision voted on by the Board: it belongs here because once passed it applies to everyone who qualifies with no further vote. Waiving a small-business fee or a fee on below-market-rate housing is a policy choice, several of these were pandemic relief, and a title that mentions a waiver may waive it for one event or one block. The sums forgone are not in the titles and, apart from First Year Free, no document on disk totals them. What would supply them: a count, from each department that collects a waived fee, of the waivers granted and their value. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
